Dana: Quick Sim FYI — ran a 6-mo capacity horizon comparing ORD vs AMS for p4d/p5d mixes.
Mike: Can you drop the numbers?
Dana: Paste of table:
```
region,gpu,type,unit_count,$/GPU_month,egress_per_tb
ORD,8,A100,8,1.20,75
AMS,8,A100,8,1.35,60
ORD,4,H100,4,1.45,90
AMS,4,H100,4,1.40,85
```
Saira: Those unit numbers include committed discount assumptions?
Dana: yes — 1yr reserved 40% for ORD, 30% for AMS (current market bids). Spot not in this sim.
Oliver: What about sustained utilization assumptions?
Dana: Sim uses 65% sustained baseline, 20% burst to spot-capacity; we model auto-bursting to a pooled burst SKU in ORD only.
Mike: Latency penalty for cross-region routing if we centralize bursts?
Saira: 10–20ms p50 added for AMS->ORD for EU customers, might affect SLAs for real-time products.
infra-bot: FYI — historical egress variance: AMS egress stable, ORD spikes 3x during platform updates.
Dana: Key takeaways: ORD wins on committed unit-cost for A100 at scale; AMS H100 slightly cheaper due to market pricing; but EU latency + data residency pushes some customers to AMS despite higher committed unit price.
Oliver: So recommendation: keep baseline reserved in ORD for A100-heavy workloads, move EU-sensitive H100 pools to AMS with smaller reserved commitment and larger burst margins.
Mike: Sounds good. Can you open a follow-up PR with exact commit numbers and risk sensitivity curves?
Dana: On it — will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
